contexts.text: A bright light beautifully turning yellow, by which was signified the first life of (a resuscitated person), namely, what is celestial with what is spiritual.
The fiery appearance of Gehenna, which is reddish, at their coming became more of a bright white...
Little children and the mothers were seen in a light of such brightness and splendour that nothing could possibly be brighter. SE 3389.
Under Colour, see this reference, and at AC 4530. AC 9865:2.
Knowing that their souls are white...
They appear to themselves in white and bright [garments].
Under Face, see this reference.
Whiter than snow, and whiter than milk () = in celestial truth... Whiteness, and whiteness, are predicated of truth. AE 364:5.
Under White, see these references. AC 9407:9. AE 196.
A heavenly proprium, which is bright and resplendent.
Under Fine linen, see this reference.
Exterior truths are represented by the brightness of the garments in Heaven; interior truths by the brightness and resplendence of the face.
Hence the Angels are in brightness and beauty ineffable...

Truths were represented by an azure colour mingled with a lovely shining whiteness; the brightness cannot be described. Appearances of truth were represented by a dim brightness; and falsities by black clouds. SE 2632. SE 2633.
Divine truth... appears as a flaming light in the inmost Heaven, and as a bright white light in the middle one. AC 9570:end. AC 9865:2. HH 128:2, Explained.
Truth of faith from good of charity is presented in Heaven by means of a bright white light.
Under Blue, see this reference.
Beautiful, bright, and angelic.

Before the left eye it does not appear as a Sun, but as a Moon, similar in whiteness, but sparkling more... than the moon of our Earth, and which is surrounded by many little moons, each of which glitters white and sparkles in the same way.
The brightness and lustre of the light of Heaven cannot be described.
The Lord appears to everyone according to his state; thus... bright white when their love departs.
The less intelligent Angels have bright white and dead white garments devoid of resplendence.
Both bright white and dead white correspond to truth. References.
A flaming and bright light...
The light with the Angels of the higher Heavens is so white that it cannot be described, not even by the whiteness of snow...
By a white colour is signified the truth of wisdom... The reason a white colour signifies the truth of wisdom is that it derives its origin from the light...
A coat of white wool.
The white colour signifies the intelligence of the husband...
Like taking away the whiteness from the ruddiness of the face...
Hatreds appear like dusky fires, and revenges like bright fires.
Charity is red from the flame of spiritual fire, and faith glitters white from the resplendence of the light therefrom.
Faith is as white as snow, and as white as water.
A dusky spirit may dwell under a bright face.
Spiritual things are represented by... white things, and by shining ones; and when what is celestial reigns, by resplendently bright ones.
A colour... like that of the blood, either white, or red.
They seem to become white, like swine, by the scraping off of their bristles.
Of a beautiful human whiteness...
An infant clothed in a white garment...

On the brightness of innocence... This brightness is so distinguished from dead white that it ought not to be compared to it; what is snowy approaches the appearance of it; but still it is such brightness as cannot be described.
Such are represented by a priest clothed in a black garment, who has a bright cloud [around him], and afterwards by a bright virgin... But that brightness was taken away from him.
His head and hairs white () = the Divine in first principles and ultimates... White = pure. That white, and white = what is pure, References.

As white wool, as snow () = as to good and truth there... That snow = truth in ultimates is from the water which is the source of it, and from its whiteness, and brightness... That whiteness, and brightness = truth, from the transparency of light, References. AE 197:4.
White () is predicated of truth; in like manner snow; and bright, of the good of truth; in like manner milk.
